item.description: Australia's Indigenous population was up to seven times larger before colonisation than previously estimated, but was devastated following the arrival of Europeans, new research reveals. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Australia’s Indigenous population estimated at 2.2m before ‘demographic catastrophe’ of colonisation
item.description: Study finds earlier numbers were underestimated, suggesting impact of diseases and massacres were much greater than previously thought Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The number of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in Australia before colonisation was dramatically underestimated, according to new research that suggests many more of them were killed. Modelling by a national research group puts the population levels before the 1788 first fleet arrived at 2.2 million, compared with early estimates of 250,000 people. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Tory Shepherd

item.title: Indigenous Australian population was much larger than previously thought and decimated after First Fleet's arrival
item.description: Australia had a much larger Indigenous population before the arrival of Europeans than previously thought, according to new research. The research also demonstrates much larger population losses resulting from colonization than previously believed, with an estimated 93% of the pre-European population lost in less than 80 years following the 1788 arrival of the First Fleet. Fuente: Phys.org.
